text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-pool-us-west1 — multiple kubelet restarts detected (3 nodes). Elevated 5xx for /v1/generate. PagerDuty: oncall (primary) paged.
Aisha (oncall): I'm on it. ACKing pager. Anyone already looking at dashboards?
Ben (sre): Seeing pod churn in namespace 'inference'. A bunch of pods in CrashLoopBackOff with GPU allocation failures. 5xx spike to ~12% for the last 5m.
Ben (sre): quick dump: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|Evicted"` shows ~18 affected pods across nodes gpu-usw1-0{2,4,7}.
Carlos (runtime): Grabbed one pod log:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
GPU 0: failed to allocate 524288000 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve.py", line 212, in handle_request
    with model.allocate_gpu(batch):
  File "/opt/runtime/cuda_utils.py", line 87, in allocate_gpu
    raise RuntimeError("CUDA OOM")
```

Maya (infra): node-level dmesg on gpu-usw1-02 shows GPU reset and NVRM messages: `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:02:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.` likely hardware/driver resets.
Aisha (oncall): Can we confirm kubelet restart reason? `kubectl describe node gpu-usw1-02` gives: `kubelet: process crashed, restarted by systemd` and `Last seen: 3m`
Ben (sre): Also saw container runtime error earlier: `failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: caused by: unable to start container process: fork/exec: cannot allocate memory` — looks like memory pressure + GPU resets.
Maya (infra): I'm SSH-ing into node to check journald and driver logs. Running `journalctl -u kubelet -b -1 | tail -n 80` now.
Maya (infra): `nvidia-smi` on healthy node: stable. On gpu-usw1-02: GPUs show `No devices were found` right after reset. dmesg indicates PCIe link flaps. Could be firmware/driver + kernel combo.
Carlos (runtime): Short-term mitigation: reduce model footprint and divert traffic to a smaller model variant to avoid GPU OOM. Can we flip a routing rule?
Aisha (oncall): Agree. Deploy-bot, can we switch inference-route 'text-gen' to fallback-model v1-small for 15m?
deploy-bot: Accepted. Rolling config change: `route:text-gen -> model:v1-small` starting now.
Aisha (oncall): I'll cordon the flapping node to stop scheduling new pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-usw1-02` — doing it now.
Ben (sre): Cordon done. Next: avoid draining to prevent mass restarts; instead scale up nodes in pool to absorb traffic. Maya, can you bump autoscaling target?
Maya (infra): Increasing pool min from 3 -> 6 for inference-us-west1 via autoscaler (GKE) now. This should create fresh nodes on new hardware. ETA ~3-4m.
Carlos (runtime): Also enabling aggressive prefix/KV cache so in-flight requests are smaller. Pushed config change to runtime: `kv_cache.enabled=true, prefix_cache_ttl=60s`
Aisha (oncall): Noted customer impact: increased 5xx and higher p99 latency. PMs notified. Patch mitigation: route->v1-small + autoscale up + cordon flappy node.
Ben (sre): Observability note: creating a temporary alert suppression for false-positive downstream alarms while we stabilize. Added silence in alertmanager for 20m.
Maya (infra): New nodes are provisioning. kubectl get nodes shows gpu-usw1-10..13 in Ready state. Pods are being scheduled there.
Ben (sre): After route switch and scale up, 5xx dropped to ~1.5% and p99 latency decreased. Looks like mitigation working. :thumbsup:
Aisha (oncall): For the flappy nodes, we should restart kubelet once driver is stable. I'm going to collect packaging: driver version, kernel, node image, and open a tracking ticket.
Maya (infra): Collected node metadata: gpu-usw1-02: kernel 5.4.0-116, NVIDIA driver 470.86. Node OS image patched last month. I'll schedule a controlled reboot + reinstall driver on the 3 affected hosts during the maintenance window if hardware vendor isn't needed.
Carlos (runtime): Also we should add a temporary fallback routing policy in API gateway to prefer nodes in 'new-hw' pool until we confirm stability. I pushed a canary policy: 90% to new-hw, 10% to original.
Aisha (oncall): Handing off to Carlos for ongoing stabilization and post-incident cleanup. I'm off the pager in 30m but will stay reachable.
Carlos (runtime): Taking over. Current status: traffic routed to v1-small, autoscaled up, flappy nodes cordoned. I'll keep watchers on GPU resets and kernel logs. Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-1543.
Ben (sre): Notes for postmortem: timeline, kernel/driver mismatch hypothesis, suggestion to add node-level health check for GPU PCIe link and to failover before kubelet restarts.
Maya (infra): I'll follow up with cloud provider support for hardware checks on the three nodes.
Carlos (runtime): Estimated time to resolve: 2-4 hours for full remediation (driver patch or node replacement). Immediate customer impact mitigated.
Aisha (oncall): Thanks team. Please add any follow-ups to INC-2026-1543. Adding checklist:
- [ ] Replace/repair nodes gpu-usw1-02/04/07 or reprovision on different host SKU
- [ ] Driver/kernel reconciliation test on staging
- [ ] Add GPU PCIe-link monitoring + alerting
- [ ] Postmortem + customer communication draft

Maya (infra): I'll start node replacement now as a precaution for gpu-usw1-02.
Ben (sre): Leaving small note: observed short NCCL errors earlier: `NCCL WARN Overrun` in a few logs — could be side effect of resets. Capture logs to S3 under s3://redwood-incident-logs/1924001111/
Carlos (runtime): I'll own the postmortem doc and link logs. Thanks — moving this to incident-handled state.
Aisha (oncall): Closing slack thread for now. If anything flips back, poke with @here. :white_check_mark:
